sections.h2: Which Wood County office takes my deed for recording?
sections.html:
Bring or mail it to the Wood County Recorder, whose suite is upstairs in the County Office Building at One Courthouse Square, Bowling Green. Call 419-354-9140. Staff are at the counter weekdays from half past eight until half past four.

Perrysburg was the first seat of government and Bowling Green took over in 1870; ground was broken for today's courthouse on November 28, 1893. The county covers 620 square miles beside the Maumee River and sits inside the Toledo metropolitan area. In 2020 it held 132,248 people in 53,202 households, and 65.9 percent of occupied housing units were owned by their residents. Rental homes are common as well, at 34.1 percent of occupied units.

Three county offices touch every sale. The Recorder keeps the permanent record. The Auditor changes the name on the tax rolls. The Treasurer, at 419-354-9130, is the contact for money owed on the parcel.

sections.h2: What makes a Wood County deed ready to record?
sections.html:
Start with the grantor's signature and a certificate from a notary or other authorized officer (Revised Code 5301.01). Then file with the county that contains the parcel. Under Revised Code 5301.25, an unfiled deed is treated as fraudulent against a later buyer who paid in good faith.

The Recorder's website carries document standards and a note on marginal references. A marginal reference ties a new paper to an older one through an instrument number or a volume and page. A release names the mortgage it ends. Citing the prior deed inside a deed costs nothing extra, but citing a land contract or a terminated life estate gets indexed and priced as a reference. Before mailing a deed, run down this list:

  • The signature and notary block are complete.
  • The legal description matches the previous recorded deed or a newer survey.
  • The Auditor's endorsement appears on the front.
  • The payment covers each page, including the caption page.

sections.h2: What will Wood County charge me to record?
sections.html:
Every recording charge in Revised Code 317.32 comes in matched halves, a base fee and a housing trust fund fee of the same size. Each half is $17 for the first two pages and $4 for each page after that. A county may layer a preservation surcharge of up to $5 on top. The Wood County Recorder's site includes an estimator that totals the fees for your paperwork.

Page size is eight and a half by fourteen inches, and a fraction of a page is billed as a page, so a long exhibit adds cost. The table lists the items a home seller meets most often.

Statutory recording charges, with the Wood County copy rate
ChargePrinted amount
Pages one and twoTwo halves of $17 each
Each added pageTwo halves of $4 each
County preservation surchargeCapped at $5
Reference entered by a separate instrumentTwo halves of $2 each, per reference
Copy of a recorded page in Wood County$2.00 each

Sources: Ohio Revised Code 317.32 and the Wood County Recorder contact page.

sections.h2: Why does the Auditor see a Wood County deed before the Recorder does?
sections.html:
Call the Auditor at 419-354-9150 to arrange the transfer. The buyer files a value statement, the Auditor writes the fee on the deed, and the stamped deed moves on to the Recorder. Revised Code 319.54 prices the fee as one dollar or ten cents per hundred dollars of value, whichever is more, and the seller carries it.

Commissioners may add a transfer tax capped at thirty cents per hundred dollars (Revised Code 322.02). Whether Wood County has done so is a question for the Auditor, and the answer belongs in your closing estimate.

sections.h2: How do I search Wood County records or order a copy?
sections.html:
The Recorder's site offers three search paths. Adaptable Visual Access shows the index from 1980 forward and trails the real filing date by roughly a day. A Laredo Anywhere account shows document images, but the office designed it for high volume professional users and asks for an account request form. AmeriScan's Documents-On-Demand shows the old physical book indexes.

A June 30, 2026 deadline in Revised Code 317.13 told every county recorder to post indexes and images of instruments from 1980 onward and to accept conveyances electronically. Charging a fee simply to open a login is not allowed.

Copies cost $2.00 per page. The office wants an instrument number or a book and page with every request, and staff will not open a document to look for a legal description. Before you order, note that the Recorder's home page also carries tiles for public notices, recording fees, document standards, a short office history and a bulk images service. A typical order runs like this:

  • Search the index by name and write down the instrument number.
  • Decide whether you want the whole document or only certain pages. The first or last page needs no extra identification.
  • Send the number and page choice by email or phone.

sections.h2: What do Wood County's housing and job base mean for a seller?
sections.html:
The county's 2019 financial report named Bowling Green State University (3,300 employees), Magna (2,200), First Solar (1,200), Owens Community College (1,000), Wood County Hospital (875) and FedEx Ground (800) among its biggest employers.

Libraries follow the same patchwork. The Wood County District Public Library serves Bowling Green from its main building and a Walbridge branch, while Perrysburg, Rossford, North Baltimore, Pemberville and Weston each run their own, and all share the Woodlink catalog.

sections.h2: Which Wood County cities and school districts should a seller name?
sections.html:
Four whole cities lie in the county, Bowling Green, Northwood, Perrysburg and Rossford, along with the edge of Fostoria. The county touches seven others (Lucas, Ottawa, Sandusky, Seneca, Hancock, Putnam and Henry), and a parcel near a line is filed in whichever county holds the land. Fifteen school systems draw from Wood County, and a few are easy to confuse: Eastwood, Elmwood, Lake, Otsego and Patrick Henry are local districts, while Perrysburg and Rossford are exempted village districts. Buyers who care about schools will ask which one serves the address.

The county takes its name from Captain Eleazer D. Wood, the engineer who built Fort Meigs in the War of 1812, and it was established in 1820. The Wood County Airport lies a nautical mile northeast of downtown Bowling Green, and the Maumee River marks the diagonal northwest border.

If a paid mortgage never got a recorded release, ask the lender for one and record it with a marginal reference to the original. Then call the Treasurer to learn whether any tax remains on the parcel.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee for a Wood County deed?
faqs.a: A deed of two pages carries a $17 base fee and a $17 housing trust fund fee, and each added page carries $4 and $4. If the county applies its preservation surcharge, add up to $5. The estimator on the Recorder's site gives the total for your document.

faqs.q: Does Wood County charge a transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The Auditor's conveyance fee reaches most sales, and sellers pay it. A county transfer tax exists only where commissioners enacted one, so phone the Auditor at 419-354-9150.

faqs.q: Can I order my recorded deed by phone?
faqs.a: Yes. Look up the instrument number in the online index, then call or email it in. Each page is $2.00.

faqs.q: Do Wood County's online records include old deeds?
faqs.a: The index starts in 1980 and runs about a day behind. Older records are in book indexes served through AmeriScan.

faqs.q: Who loses if a signed deed is never recorded?
faqs.a: The buyer does. Someone who later buys in good faith can come out ahead of an unrecorded deed, so the buyer should file as soon as closing ends.
